Its finally working so im good now, but this motherboard is among the worst ... I had so much trouble with this mobo its unbelievable. Its finally working so im good now, but this motherboard is among the worst I have ever used, even for its low price. Whatever i saved on the motherboard i practically spent in time and effort it took me to get it to work. It wasn't worth the effort but it works now. At first, i had purchased an amd athlon x4 840 processor, and it didn't work, despite being on the cpu list on asrock's website. I then purchased a motherboard beeper to diagnose the problem using beep codes. After plugging it in received no error code but the system would not post. I ordered a replacement twice, and even tested the cpu to make sure it worked. The motherboard still would not work with a perfectly good cpu. I finally decided to take a chance and try a different cpu. the one i tried was not on the asrock list but nonetheless, it worked, After that, the cpu is now up and running, after 2 weeks of diagnostics, 2 mobo replacements, 2 cpu replacements, 1 power supply replacement, and 2 gpu replacements, it is finally working. DON'T BUY THIS MOTHERBOARD! ITS TOO MUCH OF A HASSLE. Also, it does not come with a usb header and overclocks very low. The sound quality from onboard audio is horrible. I hear an echo from everything i watch. Also the mobo is very flexible, and installing ram with too much strength can cause the mobo to bend excessively.

Focus frustration and full of flaws Within an hour of opening the package, I had it repacked and ready for return. I knew it would not be the best optical gear ever made. They were inexpensive and they were to replace a cheap, broken pair. My binocular needs were minimal yet these failed to meet a single requirement. I did read the reviews before purchasing as I do for nearly all of my purchases. From experience, I've found most complaints are buyers who just don't have patience or cannot read directions. I typically rake them with a grain of salt. Most all negative comments regarding these binoculars are just. The optics are not clear at all. It is full of distortion. As I said, I wasn't looking for the best and I was willing to deal with lesser quality. But it was really bad. I had a toy pocket telescope/microscope when I was very young. This was almost as bad. The zoom was a laugh. As a photographer, I know zoom lenses are never as good as equally price prime lenses, but the image was very, very poor. Egonomically speaking, and the least important of my base requirements, the ease of use was far less adequate than I preferred. It was difficult to gain sufficient purchase on the focus dial so fine adjustments were nearly impossible. The zoom lever was in an odd position that required a shift from a comfortable grasp to an awkward thumb position. The most frustrating aspect was the focusing and diopter. I took awhile to get the diopter set properly. I assumed it was my failure. It took an eye crossingly long time to discover that the diopter setting would shift. After a few minutes it would fall out of focus and the eye strain began. The construction quality was fine. It was packaged fine. It was a good price. But otherwise they are useless as binoculars. That's the reason for the second star. Not even a good replacement for cheap binoculars even if your standards are low. I was shopping for telescopes and now the Celestrons are all removed from the shopping list.

This thing is so loud it will hurt your ears. Mine are ringing just like I left a rock concert. There are two volume settings. One on your blue tooth device such as your phone or tablet, and the other one is this unit itself on the multi-function controller. The controller is waterproof so you can hide your bluetooth cell phone in your pocket, and adjust the levels, and whether you want to skip to the next song, play, pause etc. Yes my ears are still ringing. What I did was turned my cell phones volume up to 10 and then turned this Boss speaker system up to 10. The problem is that when it is really loud like that what you are hearing is extremely loud distorted sound just like a rock concert. That is what makes your ears ring. By backing the volume off on your bluetooth device down to about 6, at least that was the best setting on mine, you get a very clear, clean, undistorted sound that still produces volume levels that are pretty loud. Definitely something you would hear over the roar of an ATV motor. One point I want to make is that I thought the remote for the unit was missing. Then I discovered that there is a compartment at the top that flips up. You press in the black button and everything is in there. The only things in the box are the speaker system, quick start guide, and warranty card. If you buy the  Cobra Electronics Corporation CPP 8000 Cobra JumpPack Charger  you could make this Boss Audio system completely portable for any use. The Cobra has a 12 volt female outlet that plugs directly into this Boss system male plug. Sound quality is at least an 8 or 9 out of 10 if you set the volume levels at an ideal level. Maxed out it distorts, and too wimpy it does not of course put out house rocking bass of course. The big LED light bar is very powerful. You can turn it on or off on the control panel. For a weatherproof sound box this thing sounds and performs great. If you are looking for a plug it in the wall non-waterproof boom box that tweaks this one out in sound fidelity may I recommend that  Sharp GXBT9 Portable Bluetooth Boom Box (Black)

This review is for the PowerJive [5 Pack] Assorted Lengths (6ft, 3ft,1ft) Premium Micro USB Cables High Speed USB 2.0 A Male to Micro B Sync and Charge Cables for Android, Samsung, HTC, Motorola, Nokia and More (Black Multi 5 Pack). I've probably order over 30-40 different cables from Amazon the last few years and inevitably they break (either at the neck or somewhere in the middle). Our 3 teenagers and myself are the roughest on our cables. These PowerJive cables seem built pretty well. They are thick (not thin and flimsy like some I've tried). They are backed with a lifetime warranty (I'm not sure what that covers and it doesn't say money back guarantee so could just be replacement) I tested these cables on our LG phones, our Samsung MP3 players, our tablets (Nexus 7, Kindle Fire, Kindle Fire HD - 2 different models), my Kodak PlaySport video camera, and older Blackberry. They charge quickly on almost every one of our devices. My main reasons for only a 4 star rating is that the micro USB head casing bulges just a bit and is difficult to fit in a couple of our phone and tablet cases. Most of our tablet and phone cases have very narrow openings to allow for charging cords. Also, the packaging leaves a bit to be desired as it look like they just crammed as many cords as they could in a small package to save space. Overall, I think these are great, well-made, heavy-duty Micro USB cables. Disclaimer: I received this product for free or at a discounted price in exchange for my honest review. (you can read my reviews and tell that I do not just give 5 stars because of this. Lastly, I filed a support request with Marrex through their website, detailing these apparent faults. No reply. Nada. So I'm returning it, and will try a different brand.

This brand fits the best When I ordered my ipad pro I also ordered several brands of glass screen protectors. All the brands had the same hardness scale & they all had a lifetime warranty. I started out with a different brand. It was okay although I noticed it was about 1.5mm too small around the outer edges. The other brand developed a small chipped area after 1 month. Four months later there was an 8" crack, so much for lasting a lifetime! After removing the "other" brand it was time to try JETech. It is a great fit. The protector goes right up to the edge of the screen. No 1.5mm gap. I was considering switching to the soft vinyl screen protectors after the first tempered glass protector cracked so soon. Then I remembered how difficult it is to apply the vinyl screen protectors without a flaw. I have OCD when it comes to my screen protectors. I cant stand to have a piece of dust in there. The longer you fidget with the protector, the more dust can float in. Lets face it, the application of a rigid glass protector is a lot easier. Also, the bigger the screen gets the harder it is to do a PERFECT application. So, the glass screen protector wins. If you want a perfect fit then choose this brand. I love looking at that big, beautiful, 12.9" retina display through shiny glass instead of a matte vinyl screen protector. The texture is also s-m-o-o-t-h! I love it. NOTE: I was reading some of the reviews & was surprised at some of the 1&2 star ratings due to lack of clean wipes & stickers, etc. Heres a suggestion, how hard is it for you to use an address sticker or TAPE to remove flying dust during application. Also, I always have a bottle of screen cleaning solution along with the "special " cloths. How on Earth do you clean your screens without it? These people actually gave JETech a low rating for not including the supplies with the protector. Maybe JETech assumed people stocked supplies to take care of their equipment. What are you going to do? Wait until your screen is filthy & then go buy the supplies? DUH! Id rather have a lower price & use my own screen cleaning supplies than pay for JETech to include everything but the kitchen sink.

Great for traveling, anywhere you prefer a smaller footprint! I purchased two different types of cell phone stands and I like them both for different reasons. I plan on keeping both of them, but if I was only allowed to choose one of them, it would be the larger aluminum one by Anker. This one is smaller, lighter weight, made of plastic, and the other one is made from aluminum, heavier, larger, and more stable. I will leave the same review (with minor comment changes) for both of them, as there are advantages to both. Neither of them are designed to hold a cell phone or my Kindle Paperwhite eBook in an upright vertical position while the cord is plugged in as it prevents the item from doing so. In addition to them not having an opening for a cord, it would need to be elevated in some way for one to work while plugged into the phone. I looked, but didn't see any available product that had this feature. That said, I've rated this one 4 stars, the Anker is rated 5 stars. I recommend either and/or both of them depending upon what you need it for obviously. Yes, both of them can accommodate a cell phone that is attached to it provided you turn it sideways, but it takes up more room on my desk or bathroom counter in that position, and I prefer a vertical position. Here are the basic pro and cons: Pro: Black Plastic MoKo is lightweight, a smaller footprint, easily fits into a carry on bag, purse, or most shirt pockets. Sturdy, attractive and keeps your cell phone secure and stable, especially if you don't need to plug it in while in the stand, and it fits really nicely when I'm using the flexible cell phone skin protection for the Huawei Union Y538 smart phone that I purchased directly through FreedomPop. Plenty of notches to adjust viewing it in either a vertical or horizontal position. It also has non-slip pads on the bottom, which would be very useful using it on a train or airplane. Not likely to be as durable, but it's plastic, so that is to be expected. Con: Too small to hold anything other than a smart phone in the slot/stand. When I use my Armor type bulky protective cover on the cell phone, it barely fits in the groove, so not as useful to me, when I'm traveling because I prefer the thicker protection in case it drops. It's adequate for when I'm home and just want it next to me while I'm working on the computer or watching TV. The price was reasonable enough, that I decided to keep it since the Anker brand is being used for my much larger Kindle Paperwhite.

Causes Windows Explorer to freeze intermittently, and the hard drive will unmount and remount itself randomly. This is sad. I researched 4 highly rated USB to IDE/SATA adapters, and finally decided on this StarTech USB 2.0 to SATA IDE Adapter (USB2SATAIDE). Unfortunately, this is not a good product. I used this product on a Windows XP system with an old IDE hard drive. I connected the AC adapter to the drive (and waited 20 seconds for it to fully spin up like a StarTech customer service rep said in another review), and then I connected the USB cable to the computer. Each partition on the hard drive mounted as a separate drive in Windows (I saw the Autoplay popup for each drive). It seemed to be working. However, as I clicked around the directories on the hard drive in Windows Explorer, sometimes Explorer would freeze for 5-15 seconds before it finally listed the contents of a directory. This happened several times as I was clicking around all the directories on the hard drive. Very annoying. Then I decided to do hard drive surface scan, and during the scan, Windows unmounted the hard drive and re-mounted it. I could see the drive letters disappear in Explorer, and then they re-appeared and the Autoplay popups appeared again. Not good! I disconnected all the cables and reconnected them, and I encountered the same problems as before - occasional freezing in Windows Explorer and then the drives unmounting and re-mounting. You don't want the drive to be unmounting during a file transfer - that will cause data corruption. I thought maybe it was a problem with that particular hard drive, so I got another one of my old IDE drives and connected that one. Same problem - occasional freezing in Explorer and eventually the drive unmounted and remounted itself. I thought the StarTech USB adapter was defective at that point, so I had Amazon send me a replacement. I connected my old IDE hard drive to the replacement adapter, and same thing - freezes in Explorer and eventually the drive unmounted and remounted itself. This adapter is a poor product. I will have to try out one of the other brands that I researched - either Sabrent or Cable Unlimited.

Really wanted to like it, but it simply doesn't charge batteries all the way. I really, really wanted to like this charger. But after extensive testing, I unfortunately have to rate this one star. If the charger cannot bring the battery even close to a full charge, it's not doing it's basic job. The first one I received would not charge a battery on the right side at all. I contacted the seller and they sent me a replacement. The replacement will "charge" batteries on both sides, but unfortunately it does not charge them all the way, or even close. Here is what I own: -2 Canon OEM batteries -4 Newmowa batteries -2 Canon OEM chargers -1 Third party charger -This Newmowa dual charge For all 6 of my batteries, this Newmowa charger will repeatedly, consistently report these batteries as full, after charging for short while. Then, I immediately plug the same battery into either of the Canon OEM chargers, and they both consistently will report the battery is only 50-75% full, and will spend another hour charging them until it reports 100%. My other third-party charger doesn't report percentages, but will similarly spend another hour charging the same battery another hour, after the Newmowa charger. The form factor is really nice, and I really like the idea, but if it can't do the simple job of charging the battery all the way, there's no point.

Works well under Windows 7 I bought this in order to try and update the firmware on my Samsung 840 EVO mSATA drive. The adapter is simple, and it was easy to install the 840 in the mSATA socket and clip it down. I plugged it into the native SATA on my ASUS motherboard. The boot drive for that machine is a Samsung 840 EVO SATA. The mSATA was plugged into the same Intel disk controller as the SATA drive. Samsung Magician (latest version as of early April 2016) under Windows 7 Pro 64-bit detected the drive just fine, but claimed the firmware version was the latest. It correctly identified the firmware version, but he version on the website was newer by 2 revisions. I had used the same PC and Magician to update the firmware on the SATA drive. The firmware versions for the 840 EVO SATA and mSATA are unique - different version numbers. So I downloaded the ISO Linux-based updater, and attempted to update with it. It generated some kind of error, and exited. I contacted Samsung, described what I had done, and they blamed the Syba adapter, saying it had 'an incompatible controller'. I do not actually believe this, as there is no sign of any kind of disk controller chip (or any digital chip, for that matter) on the Syba board. It seems to be a form-factor adapter, with a couple of analog bits, and little else besides the mSATA socket. So, inconclusive. It works fine under Windows. I benchmarked it, and performance between the mSATAwith the Syba and the SATA were similar. But - Big Props to Samsung on their handling of the firmware issue. Someone answered the phone immediately (and they spoke perfect, native English), they understood all the technical information that I provided, and willingly set up an exchange. They sent me a pre-paid overnight label for UPS, and had the thing back (the original drive, actually, just updated properly) in three days. The E-Mail communication was top-notch. Samsung knocks it out of the park, warranty-wise, unlike Crucial. Crucial's tech support and warranty support is abysmal - worst I have seen in many years. I found this out due to a failure of an M4 drive that my Dad bought. Meanwhile, I have owned multiple Samsung SSDs, and zero problems. The firmware on the mSATA was an issue, but the manner in which they resolved the problem exceeded expectations.

The Sony  4K FDR-AX33 Camcorder Flashes Purple Color During Recording I purchased a brand new Sony FDR-AX33 4K handycam about 8 month ago (September, 2015). At first, the duration of the purple color that was covering the entire screen, like a purple filter, were short (only a few seconds). However, as time passed the purple duration prolonged and now the camcorder records mostly in purple color with short durations of normal color. I did not buy the handycam from Amazon. I got it from Costco online. It is still under the one year warranty for parts. However, I need to pay for the labor, and it may take a few weeks for repair. I am an avid photographer and videographer, and to be separated from my device at the beginning of summer hurts a lot. However, I am posting this review, so that, others may know about the flushing purple defect with the Sony FDR-AX33 (that may emerge several month after using the device). Others have also reported the problim and believe it is a defect with the sensor in some batches. Long range transmitter, audio lag, easy pairing, very good customer service I connected the Miccus in transmitter mode to the headphone output jack of my stereo receiver system and paired it with AmazonBasics Large BT speaker. It works as hoped and sounds great and pairing was no problem. It is hard to turn off unless the power is turned off. Then it stays off until turned on again. Originally I connected it to the stereo receiver system's line output but the signal was too strong with audio distortion even when the speaker volume was lowered and there is no way to decrease the output of the Miccus transmitter volume. Connecting it to the headphone output jack allows me to adjust the volume output to minimize the hum and maximize the speaker sound quality. Sounds great when properly adjusted. Great Transmitter Distance: This Miccus transmitter lets me use the AmazonBasics BT speaker outside about 40-50 feet without dropouts. Another brand transmitter with a 30 foot distance had lots of audio dropouts even at a shorter distance and I returned to Amazon. Audio Lag Noticeable: There is an audible audio lag time when compared to the wired speakers connected to the stereo receiver. With the wired speakers on and the Miccus transmitter connected to the BT speaker, the audio lag from the BT speaker is very noticeable. But the purpose of using the BT speaker is to listen to music away from the wired speakers. So the audio lag is not a problem for my use. The audio lag time might be annoying for an audio-video application where you watch a TV image and listen to the audio with a noticeable lag time. Good Customer Service: The original unit that I purchased from Amazon and sent by Gadgetsville was dead on arrival. It simply would not work even when I used my own substitute power adapter and cables. I wrote Gadgetsville ("Ask Product Question" button) to tell them that the unit would not turn on and they immediately sent me a replacement with a prepaid return envelope. The replacement worked perfectly so I cancelled my return request to Amazon. Bottom Line: I would recommend the Miccus in transmitter mode for audio-only applications (without a video). The distance is great, there is no adjustment for transmission strength,

Good headphones (for a while...Edited review) Very happy with this purchase. I was worried they would be too big, since I have a very small head, but on the smallest setting, they fit comfortably. I also wear glasses, and am pleased to report that I can wear these headphones all day long at work without getting any pain or discomfort around my ears, and the ear cups are big enough to fit all the way around my ears. Sound quality is great, as expected from Sennheiser. These sound as good as my wired Momentums, and the Bluetooth connection is pretty solid with my Samsung Galaxy Note 4. Very minimal skipping, even when I am on a different floor and several rooms away from the phone (left the phone in my bedroom in a top corner of the house on the second floor, and it stays connected when I am in the kitchen on the first floor and opposite corner of the house). Activating the noise cancelling did not have any noticable degradation in sound quality for me, and it really does block out sounds. I was running the garbage disposal in the kitchen sink while listening to a podcast, and couldn't hear the disposal. I downloaded the CapTune app so that I could further customize the settings. With the app, you can turn off voice notification and other sounds. I turned off all the sounds so that I don't have to hear the voice telling me when devices are connected, or when the battery is low, and also to get rid of the little beeps it makes when you raise or lower the volume using the touch pad on the right ear piece. The touch controls do take some getting used to, and are a bit sensitive, so sometimes I want to skip a track, but end up accidentally pausing it instead. I expect I will get better at it with time, and I really like this feature. Have not had any phone calls while wearing these yet, so can't comment on the phone call quality. Took one star off for superficial reasons - they are not very asthetically pleasing. They only come in one color (black), and the build looks rather cheap, in my opinion. Time will tell if they hold up, or fall apart. For now, these meet all of my qualifications, and I hope they will last. Update (09/11/2017): Well...these didn't really last very long. After 6 or 7 months of perfection, these headphones basically became unusable due to constant crackling when in Bluetooth mode. I contacted Sennheiser customer service, and they suggested that I try unpairing and re-pairing the headphones from my phone (Samsung Galaxy Note 4). This did not help. The Sennheiser rep. said that the crackling problem was probably just because in urban areas there are lots of competing signals, etc. The problem with this explanation is that the headphones worked beautifully for the first several months, and I have not moved to a new area, and the crackling happens no matter where I am, even if I am using them while hiking in a very isolated and rural area. The other problem with this explanation is that my much-less-expensive wireless BlueTooth earbuds ($40 range) work perfectly even when I'm in the city, without any crackling at all. The crackling with the Sennheiser headphones started out of nowhere - there was no incident that could have caused it. The headphones have never been dropped or exposed to water or abused in any way. Very disappointed. Update 11/8/2017: I contacted Sennheiser customer service, and after suggesting a few solutions which did not fix the constant crackling/skipping, I sent them in for warranty repair/replacement. After a couple of weeks, I received a box containing a pair of headphones. There was no note or documentation beyond a small card that said the product was refurbished. So I guess they sent me a refurbished pair as a replacement? There was no explanation, and the return address was the name of a person, so it was unclear where the package even came from. Anyway, just tried out the pair they sent me, and the cracking and skipping seems even worse on this pair than on my original. They are really just unusable. I'm not sure what to do at this point beyond maybe contacting customer service again and seeing if I can just get a refund. I love the sound quality of Senns, but they just do not last long. I previously purchased a pair of Momentum 2.0 (wired), which didn't even last a year before the cord went bad and sound was only coming out of one ear. I think it is time for me to try another brand.

Works well and has standard size, but is not crumb resistant I ordered this keyboard to replace a metal-based $300 fully programmable keyboard. I had used that keyboard (and other expensive ones) for decades, in order to avoid having to retrain my hands and habits as keyboards and systems changed over the years. I also used a programmable to transition from Microsoft Windows to Apple Mac in 2003. Todays Mac operating systems have a feature for programming modifier keys (Option, Control, Command, and Caps Lock) that promises to make programmable keyboards unnecessary. (You can find this feature at System preferencesKeyboardModifier Keys (lower right).). For me, this feature's big defect is an inability to interchange the Delete and End keys to put them where my brain expects them to be. But I thought I could live with it. When my last programmable keyboard expired after a decade of use, I looked for something with a standard 104-key layout but more reasonably priced. This one seemed to have as close to standard placement and size of the keys and rows as I could find. I first bought one for a total price of $14.71 on July 29 of this year. With the aid of Apples modifier-key-interchange feature, I was able to get it to work for typing at my usual speed, except for confusing Delete and End. Out of the box, I would have given it five stars, in part for its low price. But I tend to eat while at the keyboard, sometimes compulsively. I had to replace this keyboard today, December 7, because of sticking keys. The sticking is probably due to hard crumbs from cookies that somehow got into the mechanism and stopped the space bar and a few other keys from springing back. I tried to shake the keyboard and pound on it---a tactic that often worked with the more expensive, durable keyboards. That only made things worse. So after less than five months, Im replacing this keyboard at the lower price of $12.99. If I had to replace it every five months, over ten years it could cost me 120/5 x $12.99 = $311, about the same as a programmable that ought to last that time by itself. But Im hopeful that, while I cant train my hands to learn new tricks after over forty years of writing and computing a certain way, I might train myself not to eat at the keyboard. That would give me a healthier and more sanitary lifestyle. (If I find that crumbs are not the issue, I'll try to remember to amend this review; some day when I'm bored, I'll take the old keyboard apart and see what I can find.)
